iconicAnchor.label: Super Mario Bros. game world
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The 1985 game establishes an immediately readable side-scrolling world built from a limited low-resolution graphic vocabulary, repeatable scenery, character sprites, objects, and compact status information.

sources.title: Super Mario Bros.
sources.publisher: The Strong National Museum of Play
supports: Super Mario Bros. was released for the Nintendo Family Computer and NES in 1985 and became a defining side-scrolling console game.
Its colorful, easy-to-read graphic world supports a complete game-system anchor rather than an isolated pixel icon.

sources.title: Toru Iwatani. Pac-Man. 1980
supports: Pac-Man is an early interactive flat landscape organized as a maze.
The work supports the style's emphasis on compact sprites, a bounded play field, limited high-contrast color, and screen-native information.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches screen pixel, screen scale, digital signal, play signal, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/8-bit-pixel-art/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
